title: Gideon and the Orchard
premise: Cyrus Ravensworth, a pastry chef drowning in debt and three missed lease payments from losing her café, agrees to a fake date to survive her family's reunion at the Ravensworth orchard estate — never expecting the stranger she hires, orchard heir Theo Ashcombe, to feel so real by dessert. As their staged romance deepens into something neither planned, Cyrus is offered a once-in-a-lifetime head pastry position in Paris that would save her finances but end them. When Theo discovers the arrangement was transactional and the family fortune hinges on his own arranged engagement, both must decide whether love against duty is worth the wreckage. In the final chapter, on the day her bakery lease expires, Theo buys the building's debt and hands Cyrus the deed — choosing her over the inheritance — as she chooses to stay and build a life rooted in the orchard town.
about_author: Sable Dunmore is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets during slow shifts. She now lives in an old farmhouse surrounded by apple trees, where she bakes badly and plots happily.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A brutal morning at the café: a final notice from the landlord, a walk-in freezer on the fritz, and a loyal regular who pays in poems. Cyrus tallies what she owes against what she has and comes up short in every column. Emotional beat: weary defiance — she refuses to grieve a dream still breathing.

chapters.title: The Invitation with Thorns
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Her mother calls: the annual Ravensworth-adjacent family reunion demands Cyrus attend with a partner or endure endless matchmaking with the mayor's son. Cyrus invents a boyfriend on the spot and immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: panic dressed as confidence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Counter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Ashcombe, heir to Ashcombe Orchards, wanders into the café escaping his own family's pressure — an arranged merger-engagement looming. He watches Cyrus work and feels something unclench. He orders the same pastry twice just to stay longer. Emotional beat: quiet recognition.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Over burnt espresso, Cyrus makes Theo an outrageous offer: be my fake boyfriend for one reunion weekend, I'll pay you in pastries for a year. Theo counters — he needs a plus-one too. Two liars shake hands. Emotional beat: nervous exhilaration.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They rehearse their origin story in the closed café after hours — how they met, first kiss, inside jokes — until the fiction starts feeling dangerously easy. A practice kiss lingers two seconds too long. Emotional beat: the crack where pretending becomes wanting.

chapters.title: The Orchard Gate
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Arrival at the reunion: sprawling orchards, judging relatives, Theo's icy fiancée-to-be Vivienne already circling. Cyrus performs the girlfriend flawlessly and hates how good it feels when Theo's hand finds hers. Emotional beat: impostor syndrome with butterflies.

chapters.title: Dessert Is Served
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The reunion dinner; Cyrus charms even Theo's formidable grandmother by describing pastry like poetry. Under the table, their knees touch. By dessert, Theo realizes he's stopped acting. Emotional beat: the fake date turns real and he says nothing.

chapters.title: Cider House Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Escaping the party, they sneak into the old cider house and trade true things: her father's death, his mother's disappointment, why they're both terrified of becoming their families. Almost-kiss interrupted by a searching aunt. Emotional beat: intimacy outpacing the lie.

chapters.title: Sunday Morning, Real Enough
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The reunion ends; driving home, silence in the car is louder than any performance. Neither wants the weekend to have been pretend. At her door, Theo kisses her cheek — off-script. Emotional beat: grief for something that technically never existed.

chapters.title: Paris Calls
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A legendary Paris patisserie offers Cyrus a head chef position — salary enough to erase every debt, starting in six weeks. She should celebrate. Instead she thinks of orchard light and a man who listens. Emotional beat: opportunity as a trap.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Her landlord delivers the ultimatum: full arrears in thirty days or the café goes to auction. Cyrus signs the Paris contract as a deposit hits her account — then can't bring herself to tell Theo. Emotional beat: guilt calcifying into secrecy.

chapters.title: Falling Without Permission
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A golden stretch of stolen weeks: farmers' markets, late-night baking lessons, Theo teaching her to graft apple trees. They never label it, and the unlabeled thing grows roots. Emotional beat: happiness with an expiration date.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Vivienne confronts Theo: the merger-engagement moves forward, and she's done waiting. His grandmother's health falters; the board pressures him to secure the Ashcombe legacy. Duty tightens its grip. Emotional beat: the cage he was born into, locking shut.

chapters.title: What the Photograph Showed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A reunion guest posts photos online; a comment thread leads Theo to discover the original ad-for-hire post Cyrus placed months ago. Every memory rewrites itself as transaction. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming from a misunderstanding.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo confronts Cyrus mid-shift, customers watching. She tries to explain — the lease, the debts, the fact that none of it felt fake after dessert — but he only hears 'paid.' He walks out. Emotional beat: heartbreak with the whole truth stuck in her throat.

chapters.title: Flour and Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus throws herself into baking through the night, boxing up Theo's favorite tart she'll never deliver. Her mother arrives, sees the wreckage, and tells her own story of choosing duty over love — and regretting it for forty years. Emotional beat: inherited warning.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His grandmother, sharp as ever, reveals she knew about the fake date from day one — and that she's seen how he looks now versus how he looked with Vivienne. She hands him the orchard's founding letter: legacy means planting what you love, not preserving what you fear. Emotional beat: permission granted.

chapters.title: Broken Contract
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus tears up the Paris contract, forfeiting the deposit, and drafts a letter to Theo explaining everything — the lease, the lie, the moment it stopped being one. She drives to the orchard in a storm. Emotional beat: choosing ruin over regret.

chapters.title: Storm at the Cider House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They meet at the cider house as rain hammers the roof. Shouting, then honesty: he shows her the founding letter; she shows him the torn contract. First real kiss, no script, no audience. Emotional beat: the climax — love declared against every duty.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The café lease expires; the auction begins. Cyrus attends with nothing but dignity and a plan to say goodbye properly. Bidding opens — then Theo walks in and buys the building outright, outbidding a developer with cold precision. Emotional beat: disbelief turning to fury turning to wonder.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Outside the auction house, Theo hands Cyrus the deed — no strings, no ledger, just 'I chose you.' He's walked away from the merger, risking disinheritance, and has never stood straighter. Emotional beat: love as an act of courage, not sacrifice.

chapters.title: Gideon and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. One year later: the café thrives, renamed Gideon's after her father; Theo runs the orchard his way, grandmother proud, Vivienne amicably freed. They plant a new apple variety together and name it Second Chance. Emotional beat: belonging found — roots planted where love grew.
